A1.justification: Both readable 23-page PDFs describe PaRaMS and contain the same main sections and Appendices A–J. Text and rendered-page comparisons support reliable assessment of the equations, results and presentation.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification and image-generation experiments, adaptive-attack evaluations, and appendix ablation and computational-cost results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Sections 5–6 and Appendices H–J.

M1.justification: Section 4.2 revises the stated attention-scaling updates: Q_i, K_i and V_i are multiplied by their scaling matrices on the right rather than the left, while the output-projection block receives inverse scaling on the left. This locally corrects an existing component. Appendix Algorithm 1 remains unchanged, and the PDFs do not establish an implementation change.

E1.justification: Both retain the same seven image-classification datasets, text-to-image generation scenarios, and Emotion/Twitter classification experiments with an Alpaca-finetuned merging partner. Appendix task coverage is also unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 5 retains TA, TIES, WA and AdaMerging with and without DARE; Table 3 retains TA and PEM-TA. The adaptive-attack comparisons and appendix comparator membership are unchanged.

E3.justification: The reported model configurations, merging coefficients, numbers of merged models, evaluation metrics and 1,000-image generation evaluation remain unchanged. No experimental protocol revision accompanies the equation correction.

E4.justification: Both contain identical coefficient and merging-count analyses, connectivity analysis, adaptive-attack evaluations, component ablations, computational-cost comparisons and generated-image examples.

E5.justification: Statistical reporting is unchanged. Both retain point estimates and averages without reporting repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical results in Tables 1–13 and empirical figures are unchanged, including appendix results. For example, Table 3 retains Emotion accuracy of 97.6% for MMP-(TA) and 21.4% for MMP+(TA) in both versions.

T1.justification: Section 4.2 replaces QK^T = AQ(A^-1K)^T with QK^T = QA(KA^-1)^T. This corrects the invariance identity for invertible diagonal A; the value/output scaling order is similarly corrected. These are mathematical corrections, but Appendix E retains the earlier erroneous derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of proactive protection against merging, preservation of unmerged functionality, broad applicability and resistance to adaptive attacks through additional pruning.

C2.justification: The shared-basin explanation, interpretation of experiments, adaptive-recovery limitations, pruning tradeoff and arguments about knowledge-distillation costs remain unchanged. No discussion addresses the incomplete propagation of the equation correction.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, appendix pseudocode, hardware, training settings and computational timings are unchanged. No code or data access information is added or revised.

R1.justification: The same 35 references and research positioning are retained, including the distinction between proactive merging prevention and prior watermarking or fingerprinting approaches.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v1 dated 8 March 2025 to v2 dated 29 June 2025. Prose, terminology, section ordering and appendix structure are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1–9, Tables 1–13 and Algorithm 1 retain identical displays, captions and placement. The corrected equations retain the existing layout without a presentation redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the main attention-scaling identity and update order in Section 4.2, improving the mathematical specification of functional equivalence. The benefit is limited because Appendix E and Algorithm 1 retain the old formulas, leaving an internal inconsistency. Empirical evidence and other substantive content are unchanged.
